categories.main_business_segments: Kroger operates primarily as a food and drug retailer, with its only reportable segment being retail operations, which represent 97% of consolidated sales. The company runs supermarkets, multi-department stores, and fulfillment centers under various local banners, and also includes retail pharmacies and fuel centers as part of its core business. Kroger also has a manufacturing division that produces private label products and operates alternative profit businesses such as data analytics and retail media.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Kroger leverages a seamless digital ecosystem, including online ordering, pickup, delivery, and ship-to-home services, supported by customer fulfillment centers powered by Ocado's automated smart platform. The company operates 33 food production plants (dairies, bakeries, grocery, beverage, meat, and cheese plants) to manufacture a significant portion of its private label products. Kroger also utilizes advanced data science and analytics, with over 20 years of investment in these capabilities, to drive personalization and alternative profit streams.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Kroger serves approximately 60 million households annually, targeting a broad consumer base across diverse demographics. Its primary customers are retail consumers purchasing groceries, pharmacy products, fuel, and general merchandise, both in-store and online. The company also serves consumer packaged goods partners through its retail media and data analytics businesses.
categories.geographic_coverage: Kroger operates exclusively in the United States, with 2,719 supermarkets across 35 states and the District of Columbia as of January 28, 2023. Its operations are organized geographically to respond to local market needs, and all revenues and assets are generated domestically.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kroger is primarily a downstream operator, selling finished consumer products directly to end customers through its retail stores and digital channels. It also has midstream activities through its manufacturing plants that produce private label goods, and it operates fulfillment centers for digital orders.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Kroger's strategic priorities are centered on four pillars: Fresh, Our Brands, Data & Personalization, and Seamless. The company is investing in digital transformation, supply chain automation, data-driven personalization, and alternative profit businesses. R&D efforts focus on enhancing the customer experience, expanding digital capabilities, improving operational efficiency, and supporting sustainability and climate initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: Kroger generates revenue primarily through the sale of consumer products in its supermarkets, pharmacies, and fuel centers, as well as through its online platforms. Additional revenue streams include private label product sales, data analytics services, third-party media revenue, and external sales from its food production plants.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Kroger operates in a highly competitive environment, facing competition from national, regional, and local food retailers, mass merchandisers (such as Walmart and Target), warehouse clubs (Costco), drugstores (CVS, Walgreens), and digital retailers. The company is one of the largest traditional supermarket operators in the U.S. and is positioning itself as a leading omnichannel food retailer with strong digital and data capabilities.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2022, Kroger reported total sales of $148.3 billion, a 7.5% increase over the prior year, with net earnings attributable to Kroger of $2.24 billion. Adjusted net earnings were $3.1 billion, and adjusted net earnings per diluted share grew 14.9% to $4.23. The company has demonstrated consistent sales growth, strong cash flow generation, and a commitment to returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kroger differentiates itself through its focus on fresh products, high-quality and affordable private label brands (Our Brands), personalized customer experiences driven by data analytics, and a seamless omnichannel shopping experience. The company emphasizes value, convenience, and loyalty programs (such as fuel rewards), and leverages its scale, data, and digital capabilities to create unique value for both customers and CPG partners.
